message.reasoning:
I'm planning to write a JUnit4 test class for NodeUtil that covers several static package-private and public methods, constructing Node objects manually using Token constants rather than relying on a parser.

The list of methods to test is extensive—covering boolean value checks, string/number conversions, side-effect analysis, operator precedence, node type checks, and assignment-related utilities—so I'll organize test cases method by method.

Still listing utility functions...

Given the scope constraints, I realize testing every single method exhaustively is impractical, so I'll prioritize broad coverage of the most branch-heavy, logic-dense methods like boolean/string/number value extraction and array-to-string conversion.

Still listing utility functions...

Given the scope, I'll aim for a substantial but pragmatic test file covering these methods with maybe 60-80 test methods, grouping multiple assertions per method where reasonable to keep things efficient while still exercising different branches. I need to figure out how to construct Node objects using rhino's constructor signatures for building test fixtures.

Also recalling boolean prop getters/setters, copyInformationFrom, and type/value accessors like getDouble and getString. I'm noting that addChildToBack-style methods automatically set the parent reference, and sketching small helper functions like num() and str() that wrap Node.newNumber and Node.newString for convenience.

For name nodes I'd use Node.newString(Token.NAME, "x"), string literals via Node.newString(Token.STRING, "foo"), and literal nodes like TRUE, FALSE, NULL, or VOID with a child are just constructed directly with new Node(Token.X). I'm also thinking about how NodeUtil being package-private affects test class placement, since I'll need access to its package-private methods.

I'm now planning out the actual test methods one by one, starting with getPureBooleanValue -- checking empty vs non-empty strings, zero vs nonzero numbers, and negation cases to cover the truthy/falsy logic branches.

Then for getImpureBooleanValue, I'm designing cases for assignment/comma expressions taking the last child's value, and NOT/AND/OR combining their operand values as expected.

Moving to getStringValue, I'm working out how each node type resolves to its string form -- literal strings pass through, numbers get formatted appropriately, booleans and null map to their token names, void becomes "undefined", and NOT expressions with boolean children resolve accordingly.

For arrays, I'm reasoning through how they stringify: empty arrays give an empty string, elements get joined with commas, and if any element's string value is null (like an unresolvable expression), the whole result becomes null. Object literals just become "[object Object]" and anything else defaults to null.

Now I'm moving to getNumberValue, mapping true/false/null to their numeric equivalents and handling numbers directly, then considering how void expressions with side effects should be treated.

I'm tracing through the special cases for NAME lookups (undefined, NaN, Infinity), negation handling with Infinity, and the NOT operator's fallthrough behavior when the value is unknown, confirming it ultimately returns null after breaking out of the switch. Then I move to STRING conversion and how array/object literals get parsed into numbers via their string representation, defaulting to null when that fails.

For getStringNumberValue, I'm checking edge cases like empty strings converting to zero and how hexadecimal strings get parsed, including malformed hex values resolving to NaN.

Now I'm covering signed hex strings and "infinity" variants returning null, normal decimal parsing working as expected, and invalid strings falling back to NaN. I also want to verify whitespace trimming works with various characters (tabs, newlines) and that the whitespace character checker correctly identifies Unicode space variants like non-breaking space and line/paragraph separators while rejecting regular letters. Finally, I'm working through how getFunctionName needs to inspect the node's parent and first child, so I'm setting up different FUNCTION node structures to test various naming scenarios.

For getNearestFunctionName, I extend on that by testing SET/GET/STRING/NUMBER as parent types. Then I move to isImmutableValue, checking simple literals and unary wrapping cases, plus special NAME values like undefined/Infinity/NaN, versus other expressions that aren't immutable. For isLiteralValue, I'm checking array literals recursively and regex literals with all-literal children.

For OBJECTLIT, I check the value nodes under each key for immutability, while FUNCTION depends on the includeFunctions flag and whether it's a declaration. Then isValidDefineValue checks whether a value node is a valid compiler define -- literals, simple arithmetic/unary combos of valid values, or qualified names present in the defines set, with calls and other expressions rejected. isEmptyBlock just checks whether a BLOCK node has no children or only an EMPTY child, and I'm starting to think through isSimpleOper next.

Now I'm working through mayHaveSideEffects, testing side-effect detection across node types like AND, THROW, OBJECTLIT (mutable state matters), ARRAYLIT/REGEXP, and VAR declarations with or without initializers.

Continuing to trace through NAME node cases -- whether a name has a child determines if it's flagged as having side effects -- and then FUNCTION nodes, where function expressions return false but function declarations register as true since they're statements.

For NEW and CALL nodes, side effects depend on flags like checkForNewObjects and whether constructor calls are known to be side-effect-free. The default branch handles simple operators (no side effect), assignment operators (special-cased), and falls through to true for anything unrecognized.

Given the scope of this, I'll aim for moderate test coverage rather than exhaustive: THROW, OBJECTLIT variants, ARRAYLIT, VAR/NAME, FUNCTION, NEW with both builtin and custom constructors, CALL with builtin and custom functions, and assignments — NAME assignment always true, GETPROP assignment depending on whether the value is local. Since checkForStateChangeHelper is private, I'll test through the public mayHaveSideEffects and mayEffectMutableState methods instead, starting with a constructor call using a NEW node.

I want to cover functionCallHasSideEffects next: calls to known safe functions like Math.foo return false, unknown calls return true, and non-CALL nodes should throw. Then I need nodeTypeMayHaveSideEffects for DELPROP/DEC/INC/THROW returning true, delegating CALL/NEW, checking NAME with vs without children, and default cases like ADD returning false while assignment ops return true. I also want canBeSideEffected tests for CALL/NEW, constant vs non-constant NAME, GETPROP/GETELEM, and FUNCTION expressions, plus precedence tests across token levels including verifying an unhandled token throws an Error.

Confirming Token.BLOCK isn't in the precedence switch, so calling precedence on it should throw. I'm also planning tests for value/type checks like mayBeString with numeric versus string ADD, associativity/commutativity for MUL vs ADD, assignment op mapping including an invalid-input exception case, various simple node predicates (isName, isNew, isVar, etc.), isForIn distinguishing 3 vs 4 children, and isLoopStructure/getLoopCodeBlock across FOR/DO/WHILE with a null default.

For isWithinLoop, I'm tracing how it walks ancestors: it returns true if it hits a loop structure first, but breaks and returns false if it hits a FUNCTION boundary before finding a loop. I'm building a tree where a WHILE contains a FUNCTION containing the target node, expecting false, versus a direct WHILE->BLOCK->node nesting expecting true, and I need to confirm the Node API exposes a getAncestors() method to support this traversal.

Now I'm checking isControlStructure and isControlStructureCodeBlock against various node types—FOR, IF, TRY, CATCH, SWITCH/CASE, DEFAULT—verifying which child position (first vs last) determines the code block for each, and tracing through the switch statement's grouped cases like FOR/WHILE/LABEL/WITH to see how the default fallback behaves when the parent doesn't match any handled case.

DEFAULT returns true, and the final default branch just checks that the parent is indeed a control structure before returning false—so every case in isControlStructure is actually covered, making that fallback effectively unreachable except as a safety net.

Next I want to verify getConditionExpression across node types: IF/WHILE use the first child, DO uses the last child, FOR behaves differently depending on child count (null for 3 children, the child after first for 4, else throws), CASE returns null, and anything else like BLOCK throws IllegalArgumentException.

Then I move to isStatementBlock (true only for SCRIPT/BLOCK), isStatement/isStatementParent behavior including the null-parent case throwing IllegalStateException, isSwitchCase for CASE/DEFAULT, isReferenceName requiring a non-empty NAME string, isLabelName checking type and null-safety, and isTryFinallyNode/isTryCatch logic based on child count and position.

Next I sketch out removeChild's many branches: TRY-finally with catch handlers, plain BLOCK removal via detachChildren, statement removal from a BLOCK parent, VAR nodes with multiple vs single children, LABEL and FOR node special cases replacing with EMPTY, and an else branch that throws IllegalStateException for unsupported parent/child combos. Then I move on to maybeAddFinally, checking how it adds a BLOCK when TRY lacks a finally clause versus when one already exists.

I continue through tryMergeBlock (checking BLOCK parent types like BLOCK/SCRIPT vs FUNCTION), then simpler predicate checks like isCall, isFunction, isThis, isArrayLiteral. I also cover function declaration/expression detection with different parent contexts, object method call detection via GETPROP structures, isLhs checks against ASSIGN/VAR parents, object literal key detection, and finally opToStr for converting operator tokens to their string representations.

I move through building nested trees for containsType/containsCall/containsFunction, then getVarsDeclaredInBranch which needs to exclude variables nested inside functions during traversal. I'm now working through prototype property declarations, needing to construct proper GETPROP chains with NAME and STRING nodes to represent qualified names like "Foo.prototype.bar" since getQualifiedName() relies on well-formed tree structure.

I continue checking newUndefinedNode/newVarNode structures, then TRY node handling for finally/catch blocks, followed by getFnParameters extracting the LP node from a FUNCTION's children.

For isConstantByConvention, I decide the CodingConvention interface mock is too complex to stub reliably, so I'll skip that method along with getInfoForNameNode, getFunctionInfo, and similar ones requiring uncertain dependencies.

Continuing through the remaining methods: getSourceName checks the SOURCENAME_PROP on an ancestor node, newCallNode determines FREE_CALL based on whether the target is a NAME versus GETPROP, and evaluatesToLocalValue needs coverage across many branch types like ASSIGN, COMMA, AND/OR, HOOK, INC/DEC, THIS, NAME, GETPROP/GETELEM, CALL, NEW, and FUNCTION nodes.

I'm also planning tests for getArgumentForFunction/CallOrNew with valid and out-of-range indices, and isLatin/isValidPropertyName cases covering ASCII strings, non-ASCII characters, keywords, and invalid identifiers. Given the sheer scope of this test surface, I'm aiming to produce a reasonably comprehensive but manageable set of test cases rather than exhaustive coverage of every branch.

I'll focus on methods that are self-contained and testable without needing CodingConvention or AbstractCompiler mocks, using simple Node trees for side-effect analysis, and skip or minimize coverage of methods that require JSDocInfo mocks or CodingConvention dependencies like newQualifiedNameNode or isConstantByConvention.

Now I'm writing helper static methods for constructing test nodes, relying on Token constants like TRUE, FALSE, NULL, STRING, NAME, AND, OR, HOOK, ARRAYLIT, and OBJECTLIT to build the AST structures needed for each test case.

Still listing token types...

Still listing node types...

I need to check the Node class constructors from this old Closure compiler version, recalling the overloads that take a node type plus one or two children.

Still listing Node API methods...

These defaults should be fine for the test cases, since I'm not relying on those flags being true unless local-result checks need them specifically.

Also checking that Node.tokenToName, Node.ORIGINALNAME_PROP, and Node.SOURCENAME_PROP are properly accessible from the test package since they're used within NodeUtil, but I don't think our test actually needs to call tokenToName directly.

getAncestors() should work fine since it's built by walking parent references, so as long as I construct the tree with normal child-adding methods, that chain should resolve correctly. I'm also assuming getQualifiedName() behaves the standard way, joining NAME and STRING children of GETPROP/NAME chains with dots into something like "a.b.c".

Now I'm sketching helper functions for the test file: small builders for name, string, number, boolean, null, and void nodes, plus helpers for GETPROP chains to build qualified names and for constructing CALL nodes with a target and argument list.

Adding NEW, BLOCK, and FUNCTION builders similarly, though I'm considering just inlining node construction per test for readability given the complexity. Now I want to verify that the precedence lookup throws an error for tokens not in the switch, like BLOCK, so I'm checking the full case list again.

BLOCK is confirmed absent from the switch, so using Token.BLOCK will correctly trigger the default error case. Now I'm setting up getFunctionName tests, starting with a case for an anonymous function assigned to a variable, building a FUNCTION node with an empty name...

Adding LP and BLOCK children...

For that case, getFunctionName should traverse to the parent NAME node and return its string, "x". Next I'm setting up an ASSIGN case where a qualified name like obj.prop is assigned an anonymous function, building a GETPROP node for the left-hand side.

For this, getFunctionName should walk the assign's first child and get its qualified name, yielding "obj.prop". Then I'm checking the default case: a named function declaration attached directly under a SCRIPT node, where the function's own name node gives "myFunc" as expected.

Now I'm testing an anonymous function used as an immediately invoked call, like `(function(){})()`, where the parent is CALL rather than NAME or ASSIGN—here getFunctionName should hit the default branch with an empty name string and return null. That covers all three switch branches plus the default case's named and anonymous sub-branches. Next I want to extend getNearestFunctionName to also check SET/GET/STRING/NUMBER parents for when getFunctionName returns null on an anonymous function whose parent is CALL.

I set up an OBJECTLIT node with a STRING key holding a function value: the key's string is "foo", and after attaching the anonymous function as its child, getFunctionName sees the parent is the STRING key (not NAME/ASSIGN), falls to default with an empty name, returns null—then getNearestFunctionName detects the parent type is STRING and returns "foo" directly, confirming that branch. Similarly for a NUMBER key like `1`, getNearestFunctionName should return "1" via getStringValue on the parent when the parent type is NUMBER.

Now I'm confirming the default case where the parent doesn't match any of these types (e.g., a CALL parent), which correctly returns null since neither switch matches. With that logic settled, I want to move to drafting the actual test class—likely around 60-70 test methods—checking that NodeUtil's methods are package-private and accessible since the test class shares the same package, and making sure I import Node, Token, and TernaryValue from their respective rhino packages.

I'm verifying that TernaryValue comes from com.google.javascript.rhino.jstype, matching the source's import. I also note that methods like isNoSideEffectsCall and getSideEffectFlags are public Node methods I likely won't call directly, and that AbstractCompiler doesn't need to be referenced since tests can pass null for the compiler argument in single-arg wrapper calls.

Now I'm working through the toString() case: since callNode.hasOneChild() checks the call node's total child count (just the target with no extra args), building `x.toString()` with a GETPROP target and no arguments should make functionCallHasSideEffects return false, so I'm setting up that test case, followed by a similar one for Math.abs().

Testing an unknown object method call with an argument (like `obj.doSomething(1)`) should fail the hasOneChild check and fall through to returning true by default. I'm also verifying that calling a built-in function name like Array() correctly returns false since it's in the whitelist of side-effect-free functions.

For constructor calls, `new Array()` should return false since Array is in the side-effect-free constructor set, while `new Foo()` should return true since it's not recognized.

Then checking nodeTypeMayHaveSideEffects: delete/decrement/increment/throw nodes always report side effects, a bare NAME node doesn't but one with a child does, CALL and NEW nodes delegate to the earlier functions, ordinary ops like ADD default to false, and assignment operators are flagged true before even reaching the switch statement.

For canBeSideEffected, I'm testing that CALL/NEW nodes and non-constant NAME nodes report true, constant NAME nodes report false unless present in a supplied knownConstants set, GETPROP/GETELEM report true, function expressions report false, and other node types recurse into their children to check.

Now I'm putting together the full test file with helper methods and grouped test cases, adding comments where behavior is uncertain, and finishing with a summary table mapping test methods to the branches they cover.

For an array literal with side effects, I'm checking how mayHaveSideEffects handles an ARRAYLIT node containing a CALL element, tracing through the switch case to see whether it breaks out and falls into the general child-checking loop.

When it falls through without returning inside the case, it hits the final "return TernaryValue.UNKNOWN" after the switch, matching my expectation. For the NOT case, I'm checking that a TRUE child value gets inverted to "false" via getPureBooleanValue and toBoolean logic.

For NOT applied to an unknown value like a NAME node, getPureBooleanValue returns UNKNOWN, which skips the if and falls through to the final null return -- so getStringValue(NOT(name("x"))) should be null. Similarly a default case like ADD falls through to null since no case matches it. Now I'm moving on to check isLiteralValue for OBJECTLIT nodes, whose children are typically STRING/NUMBER/GET/SET entries.

For each key node, the value is its single child, so I test one key with a literal number value, expecting isLiteralValue to return true, then add a second key with a non-literal value like a NAME node, expecting the overall result to flip to false. For REGEXP, I test a node with no children, which trivially returns true since the loop finds nothing, then test one with a non-literal child like a CALL, expecting false even though it's not fully realistic behavior.

For ARRAYLIT with includeFunctions true, a function expression child should pass since it's an expression not a statement; with includeFunctions false, that same array should fail since functions aren't immutable by default. I also check that sparse arrays with EMPTY slots are skipped correctly, so an array with an EMPTY and a literal number still returns true.

Now I have enough coverage mapped out, so I'll start writing the actual Java test code, including a helper to build anonymous function nodes for use as statements versus expressions.

For expression context I can wrap the function as the callee of a CALL node, so its parent isn't a statement position, making isFunctionExpression true. Then for hoisted declarations I need to check whether the parent is SCRIPT or whether the parent's parent is a FUNCTION, meaning the function is nested directly inside another function's body block.

For the third test case, I need fn declared inside a plain BLOCK that isn't inside a function or SCRIPT—like a nested block within an if statement—so both conditions should be false. But if I build an unattached BLOCK as fn's parent, checking the grandparent's type will throw a null pointer exception since that BLOCK has no parent itself; I need to rely on the short-circuit evaluation of the OR to avoid this.

Actually, to sidestep the NPE entirely, I'll wrap the outer BLOCK inside an IF node so it has a real parent of type IF, not FUNCTION—giving a clean false result without crashing.

Next I'm setting up isEmptyFunctionExpression tests: an empty BLOCK body should return true, and I'm noting that a block containing only EMPTY-type children still counts as empty, while one with an actual statement like an expression result returns false. Then I move on to testing isVarArgsFunction by building a function that references "arguments" inside its body.

Now I need to test that isVarArgsFunction correctly excludes nested functions—if an inner function references "arguments" but the outer one doesn't, the outer function should still register as false, since the traversal predicate MatchNotFunction stops descending into any FUNCTION node's children, meaning references inside nested functions are never seen by the outer scan.

Good, that confirms the MatchNotFunction predicate behavior. Given the enormous scope, I'll finalize now with comprehensive but bounded coverage, skipping a few overly complex methods that require heavy JSType/FunctionType mocking, noting those with a comment instead.

I'll also skip the two-argument mayEffectMutableState overload and just test the single-arg version, relying on the standard Rhino Node constructors used throughout the source for building test nodes.

I'm fairly confident this multi-child Node constructor pattern (like the HOOK example with cond/then/else) is standard in this codebase, so I'll trust it compiles. I also confirm addChildToBack returns void and that Node.newString(type, str) is the correct helper matching our name/str utilities.

Now I'm working through the TernaryValue comparisons (TRUE/FALSE/UNKNOWN with not/and/or/toBoolean/forBoolean) for assertions against NodeUtil.getPureBooleanValue, and double-checking Node.getDouble() for numeric values from newNumber. Then I'm tracing through the hex-string parsing logic: "0x1A" parses correctly to 26.0 via Integer.parseInt with radix 16, while malformed hex like "0xGG" throws a NumberFormatException that gets caught and returns null.

I'm also checking signed-hex inputs like "+0x1" and "-0x1" which get rejected early by the sign-checking logic. For infinity strings, I'm noting the case-sensitivity issue -- lowercase "infinity" returns null, but "Infinity" with a capital I actually falls through to Double.parseDouble, which successfully parses it as positive infinity, contrary to what I'd expect from the earlier checks.

I'm working through more test cases: normal decimals parse fine, non-numeric strings like "abc" yield NaN, and whitespace-only strings trim to empty and parse as 0.0. I also want to verify the whitespace-trimming helper and character-classification function, then move on to testing numeric/boolean result detection across AND/OR/ternary combinations, starting with addition of two numbers.

For string-plus-number addition, I trace through how "may be string" gets determined for the string operand versus the number operand, confirming that when either side of an addition could be a string, the overall result can no longer be guaranteed numeric.

I then move to testing the ternary operator, verifying that a numeric result requires both branches (then and else) to independently satisfy the numeric predicate, and set up a case with a variable condition and two numeric literals. Next I check the AND operator, where a boolean result requires both operands to pass the boolean predicate, testing with two equality comparisons.

I confirm the AND boolean check fails correctly if one operand isn't boolean, then verify that ASSIGN and COMMA operators only evaluate the type predicate on their last child. With enough coverage mapped out, I'm ready to write the final test class, consolidating trivial one-liner checks into fewer methods with multiple assertions to keep things manageable within the length constraints.
